AI.method: The review covers intelligent vision for shipboard video stabilization, visual perception enhancement, object detection and tracking, and navigable area segmentation, then vision-centered fusion with infrared-visible, radar-vision, LiDAR-vision, AIS-vision and other sensors.
AI.result: The review summarizes open-source maritime datasets and safety-critical applications; the abstract reports no new quantitative results.
AI.conclusion: The paper highlights open challenges and future research directions for intelligent ship navigation and intelligent waterborne transportation systems, and its collected datasets will be regularly updated.

title: DualCast: Dual-Image Conditioned Diffusion Transformers for Digital Human E-Commerce Video Generation
summary: Digital human e-commerce video generation requires preserving product appearance, human identity, and overall video style during dynamic demonstrations. Although recent models support multiple reference images, their general conditioning schemes do not explicitly distinguish the asymmetric roles of "what is presented" and "who presents it." Consequently, generated videos may favor a single reference, resulting in product distortion, identity drift, or single-reference collapse. To address this issue, we propose DualCast, a role-addressed dual-image conditioning framework for video generation. By explicitly modeling the distinct roles of product and human conditions, DualCast reduces role ambiguity and feature competition between references. First, a dual-spatiotemporal slot injection mechanism VAE-encodes the product and human images separately and places their latent features at the front and rear boundaries of the DiT sequence, enabling sequence-level condition separation and directed injection. Second, a mask-guided region-weighted loss strengthens supervision over product, face, and product-face overlap regions, improving generation fidelity in critical areas. Third, image condition dropout enables a single model to support dual-image, product-only, and human-only generation. In addition, we construct a curated dataset of 10K e-commerce videos for model training. Experimental results demonstrate the strong performance of DualCast.

AI.tldr: DualCast is a role-addressed dual-image conditioned diffusion transformer for digital human e-commerce video that keeps product appearance and human identity separate. It also introduces a curated dataset of 10K e-commerce videos for training.
AI.motivation: General multi-reference conditioning does not distinguish what is presented from who presents it, so generated videos may favor a single reference, causing product distortion, identity drift or single-reference collapse.
AI.method: Dual-spatiotemporal slot injection VAE-encodes the product and human images separately and places their latents at the front and rear boundaries of the DiT sequence. A mask-guided region-weighted loss emphasizes product, face and product-face overlap regions, and image condition dropout lets one model support dual-image, product-only and human-only generation.
AI.result: The abstract states that experimental results demonstrate strong performance, without naming specific metrics or baselines.
AI.conclusion: Explicit modeling of the distinct product and human roles reduces role ambiguity and feature competition between references in digital human video generation.

title: Feature Puzzles: Single-Image Supervision for Multi-View 3D-Aware Segmentation
comment: Feed Forward 3D Reconstruction and Spatial Understanding, Multi-view Promptable Segmentation, Instance Tracking
summary: Humans can easily recognize the same objects across different viewpoints of a 3D scene, whereas teaching models such multi-view-consistent perception typically requires videos or calibrated multi-view captures, which are considerably more expensive and less diverse than large-scale monocular data.~In this paper, we introduce Feature Puzzles, a novel framework for learning multi-view-consistent segmentation using only single-image semantic segmentation supervision. Specifically, we propose a simple yet effective pipeline that constructs multi-view-consistent segmentation pseudo-labels through image cropping and geometric transformations. We further introduce a lightweight, plug-and-play network that leverages the multi-view-consistent image features learned by existing pretrained 3D foundation models and the generated pseudo-labels to perform multi-view-consistent segmentation. Importantly, our flexible framework supports various types of prompts provided from one or multiple views and can be readily extended to open-vocabulary 3D segmentation. Under this single-image supervision, our feed-forward model achieves the best mIoU on NVOS, remains competitive on SPIn-NeRF and ScanNet++ against baselines using per-scene optimization or in-domain multi-view training, and demonstrates zero-shot transfer to open-vocabulary 3D segmentation. Visual comparisons are available on our project page: this https URL

AI.tldr: Feature Puzzles learns multi-view-consistent 3D-aware segmentation from single-image semantic segmentation supervision alone, using pseudo-labels built through image cropping and geometric transformations. It supports prompts from one or multiple views and extends zero-shot to open-vocabulary 3D segmentation.
AI.motivation: Multi-view-consistent perception normally requires videos or calibrated multi-view captures, which are considerably more expensive and less diverse than large-scale monocular data.
AI.method: Multi-view-consistent segmentation pseudo-labels are built through image cropping and geometric transformations. A lightweight plug-and-play network uses multi-view-consistent features from existing pretrained 3D foundation models together with these pseudo-labels to perform segmentation.
AI.result: The feed-forward model achieves the best mIoU on NVOS, stays competitive on SPIn-NeRF and ScanNet++ against baselines that use per-scene optimization or in-domain multi-view training, and transfers zero-shot to open-vocabulary 3D segmentation.
AI.conclusion: Single-image supervision suffices to learn multi-view-consistent 3D-aware segmentation that is competitive with methods trained on richer multi-view data.

title: Chronos: Sequential Identity-Preserving Video Generation by Temporal Anchoring
comment: Accepted by ACM MM 2026. 1st place in Tracks 1 and 2 of the ACM MM 2026 Identity-Preserving Video Generation Challenge
summary: Identity-preserving video generation aims to synthesize high-quality and visually realistic videos from textual and visual conditions while faithfully maintaining the subject's identity across diverse motions. Prior methods have extensively introduced reference-guided control signals and identity-aware conditioning to improve facial alignment from reference images. However, improving static identity alignment alone creates a fundamental tension between identity fidelity and temporal controllability, which frequently causes identity drift or motion suppression under large pose variations and multi-segment sequential actions. To address this, we propose Chronos, a framework that unifies single-segment facial identity preservation and multi-segment sequential action generation under a common temporal formulation. Specifically, Chronos integrates Semantic Prompt Anchoring to adaptively refine the user prompt, Visual Frame Anchoring to transform conditions into visually grounded keyframe anchors for visual guidance, and Metric-Guided Candidate Routing to select the highest-quality videos from heterogeneous generators via multi-dimensional evaluation. Extensive evaluations demonstrate the superiority of our approach, which achieved first place in both Track 1 and Track 2 of the ACM MM 2026 Identity-Preserving Video Generation Challenge, demonstrating its effectiveness across both facial identity preservation and sequential action generation settings.

AI.tldr: Chronos is an identity-preserving video generation framework that unifies single-segment facial identity preservation with multi-segment sequential action generation through temporal anchoring. It won first place in both Track 1 and Track 2 of the ACM MM 2026 Identity-Preserving Video Generation Challenge.
AI.motivation: Improving static identity alignment creates a tension with temporal controllability, causing identity drift or motion suppression under large pose variations and multi-segment sequential actions.
AI.method: Semantic Prompt Anchoring adaptively refines the user prompt, Visual Frame Anchoring turns conditions into visually grounded keyframe anchors, and Metric-Guided Candidate Routing selects the highest-quality videos from heterogeneous generators via multi-dimensional evaluation.
AI.result: First place in both Track 1 and Track 2 of the ACM MM 2026 challenge, covering facial identity preservation and sequential action generation; the abstract gives no numerical metrics.
AI.conclusion: The common temporal formulation is effective across both identity preservation and sequential action generation settings.

title: DecoupAttn: Decoupled Sparse Attention for Training-Free Acceleration of Video Diffusion
summary: Sparse attention accelerates few-step video diffusion transformers by computing a few key blocks exactly and compensating for the rest. However, existing sparse attention still faces key challenges, including identification overhead from finding critical blocks at every denoising step, suboptimal budget allocation that sets sparsity budgets uniformly or by local metrics, and cross-step error accumulation as reused masks or clusters go stale. Observing that the errors left on skipped blocks cancel each other once every key is compensated, we propose DecoupAttn, a new paradigm of decoupled sparse attention: semantic clusters compensate every key, and exact attention corrects their error on a few blocks fixed once offline by position. To support this paradigm, we introduce Distortion Budget, a rate-distortion objective for budget allocation that places exact computation across timesteps, layers, and heads where it removes the most distortion that compensation leaves in the final latent. Built on this budget, we further propose Reassign Cache, in which each step reassigns the drifting keys to cached centroids and refreshes compensation while the budgeted blocks stay fixed. Moreover, DecoupAttn is training-free: a few calibration clips compile one plan offline, and inference runs standard block-sparse kernels with one fused compensation kernel. Our code will be released after submission.

AI.tldr: DecoupAttn is a training-free sparse attention method for few-step video diffusion transformers that compensates every key with semantic clusters and corrects errors on a few position-fixed blocks. It allocates exact computation with a rate-distortion budget and reassigns drifting keys to cached centroids.
AI.motivation: Existing sparse attention suffers from identification overhead at every denoising step, from budgets set uniformly or by local metrics, and from cross-step error accumulation as reused masks or clusters go stale.
AI.method: Decoupled sparse attention pairs semantic-cluster compensation for every key with exact attention on a few blocks fixed once offline by position. Distortion Budget is a rate-distortion objective that places exact computation across timesteps, layers and heads, and Reassign Cache reassigns drifting keys to cached centroids each step, with one fused compensation kernel and standard block-sparse kernels at inference.
AI.result: The abstract reports no quantitative speedup or quality numbers.
AI.conclusion: Because errors on skipped blocks cancel once every key is compensated, a budget fixed offline from a few calibration clips makes the acceleration training-free.

title: 3D Banff Glomerulitis Scoring for Kidney Transplant Pathology: Feasibility Study for Volumetric Quantification
summary: Quantifying glomerular inflammation in kidney-transplant biopsies is traditionally performed on single whole-slide sections using the Banff "most-severe section" rule, despite the inherently three-dimensional nature of lesion distribution. This 2D based assessment might lead to instability when inflammation varies across slices. This paper reports a feasibility study examining the technical feasibility and clinical relevance of extending Banff scoring into three dimensions. To this end, we propose a 3D Banff lesion-scoring framework that aligns serial sections, reconstructs glomerular identities across depth, and integrates inflammatory-cell counts in 3D under three scoring strategies: Compatible, Volumetric, and Deduplicated Volumetric. In the experiments, glomerulitis (g-scores) was used as an example Banff metric and applied to multi-section renal allograft biopsies. Our findings indicate that 3D Banff g-scores are more consistent across sections and, under the semi-automatic setting, the Volumetric strategy correlates more strongly with clinical biomarkers than traditional 2D scores. These results show that 3D volumetric quantification offers promising added value, underscoring the potential benefit of 3D-aware Banff scoring for kidney transplant pathology.

AI.tldr: This feasibility study extends Banff glomerulitis (g-score) scoring of kidney transplant biopsies from single 2D sections to 3D volumes. In the semi-automatic setting, the Volumetric strategy correlates more strongly with clinical biomarkers than traditional 2D scores.
AI.motivation: The Banff most-severe-section rule scores inflammation on one whole-slide section, which can be unstable when inflammation varies across slices, although lesion distribution is inherently three-dimensional.
AI.method: A 3D Banff lesion-scoring framework aligns serial sections, reconstructs glomerular identities across depth, and integrates inflammatory-cell counts in 3D under three strategies: Compatible, Volumetric and Deduplicated Volumetric. Glomerulitis serves as the example metric on multi-section renal allograft biopsies.
AI.result: 3D g-scores are more consistent across sections, and under the semi-automatic setting the Volumetric strategy correlates more strongly with clinical biomarkers than traditional 2D scores.
AI.conclusion: Volumetric quantification offers added value, supporting 3D-aware Banff scoring for kidney transplant pathology.

title: FLINT: Coupling Proximal Initialization and Bounded Stochasticity for Flow-Matching Inverse Problems
comment: NeurIPS 2026, Project Page: this https URL
summary: Flow matching models have emerged as a dominant paradigm for generative posterior sampling in imaging inverse problems. Existing solvers follow two distinct lines of work: trajectory-space methods, which refine sampling dynamics from random initial noise, and source-space methods, which optimize the initial noise itself. While most prior work treats these as independent design choices, we show that they are inherently coupled. We derive a unified stability bound that links initialization proximity and cumulative sampling stochasticity through a multiplicative envelope, complemented by two empirical observations. First, we identify a sufficiency regime in which a moderately optimized proximal source initialization is enough to attain the performance plateau, rendering exhaustive source-space optimization unnecessary. Second, this initial advantage is fragile: it is eroded by excessive stochasticity accumulation during guided sampling, necessitating a mechanism that bounds the cumulative noise injection. These findings motivate FLINT, a two-stage framework that operationalizes this coupling. FLINT establishes a high-fidelity starting point via a manifold-constrained proximal objective in only a few iterations, then performs guided sampling under a bounded stochasticity schedule that helps prevent erasure of the initialization advantage. Across diverse inverse problems, FLINT delivers state of the art perceptual quality and competitive distortion metrics while maintaining superior computational efficiency.

AI.tldr: FLINT is a two-stage flow-matching solver for imaging inverse problems that first computes a proximal source initialization in a few iterations, then runs guided sampling under a bounded stochasticity schedule. It reports state-of-the-art perceptual quality and competitive distortion across diverse inverse problems.
AI.motivation: Trajectory-space and source-space solvers are usually treated as independent design choices, but a unified stability bound shows that initialization proximity and cumulative sampling stochasticity are coupled, and excessive stochasticity erodes the initialization advantage.
AI.method: A manifold-constrained proximal objective establishes a high-fidelity starting point in only a few iterations, and guided sampling then runs under a bounded stochasticity schedule that limits cumulative noise injection.
AI.result: FLINT delivers state-of-the-art perceptual quality and competitive distortion metrics across diverse inverse problems while maintaining superior computational efficiency.
AI.conclusion: Coupling proximal initialization with bounded stochasticity is a practical design for posterior sampling, and in the sufficiency regime exhaustive source-space optimization is unnecessary.

title: CLEAR: Color-Texture Latent Alignment for Single Image Reflection Removal
summary: Single Image Reflection Removal (SIRR) seeks to recover the transmitted scene from a photograph captured through glass. Recent latent restoration methods use pretrained generative priors, but many recover detail by feeding high-frequency features from the degraded input back into the decoder. This works for degradations such as blur, noise, or haze, where input detail mostly belongs to the scene. It is less suitable for SIRR, where reflections add a second structured layer: directly reusing the input's skip connections can sharpen the image while also bringing reflection edges back. Latent compression also introduces color drift and fine-detail loss. We propose CLEAR (Color-Texture LatEnt Alignment for Single Image Reflection Removal), a deterministic, single-timestep, non-iterative latent framework that uses a pretrained latent diffusion backbone as a natural-image prior. A physics-guided separator organizes the prediction around the transmission, reflection, and residue formation model and outputs coarse layer latents in one forward pass. The Hybrid Feature Alignment Module (HFAM) then treats input-derived skips as contaminated layer-mixture features. It rectifies their high-frequency content with a clean-transmission-aligned color query, learned from the input features themselves under ground-truth feature supervision, keeping transmission-consistent texture while attenuating reflection-colored detail. CLEAR achieves the best average across fidelity and perceptual metrics on six real-world benchmarks and the lowest LPIPS on every dataset, with the largest gains on the hardest benchmarks.

AI.tldr: CLEAR is a deterministic, single-timestep latent framework for single image reflection removal that uses a pretrained latent diffusion backbone and aligns the color and texture of input skip features. It achieves the best average across fidelity and perceptual metrics on six real-world benchmarks and the lowest LPIPS on every dataset.
AI.motivation: Latent restoration methods feed high-frequency input features back through skip connections, which suits blur, noise or haze but reintroduces reflection edges in reflection removal, and latent compression causes color drift and fine-detail loss.
AI.method: A physics-guided separator organizes the prediction around the transmission, reflection and residue formation model and outputs coarse layer latents in one forward pass. The Hybrid Feature Alignment Module treats input-derived skips as contaminated layer-mixture features and rectifies their high-frequency content with a clean-transmission-aligned color query learned under ground-truth feature supervision.
AI.result: Best average across fidelity and perceptual metrics on six real-world benchmarks and the lowest LPIPS on every dataset, with the largest gains on the hardest benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Aligning skip features to the clean transmission keeps transmission-consistent texture while attenuating reflection-colored detail.

title: PathoS2VD: From 2D Histopathology to Pseudo Z-Stack Representations
summary: For decades, diagnostic pathology has relied on thin two-dimensional (2D) tissue sections, despite biological tissues exhibiting inherently three-dimensional (3D) morphological organization. Because a single section captures only one focal plane, important morphological cues along the z-axis are inevitably discarded, limiting tissue representation for both human interpretation and computational analysis. In this work, we propose a generative framework that learns z-axis morphological priors from pathology z-stack data, offering a cost-effective alternative to dedicated volumetric imaging, and transfers this knowledge to conventional single-plane histopathology. Specifically, an image-to-video (I2V) latent diffusion model (LDM) is trained to synthesize a pseudo z-stack from a single 2D image, capturing plausible morphological variations across adjacent focal planes rather than reconstructing physical tissue volumes. To enable deployment on large-scale clinical datasets without native z-stack acquisition, we further introduce a prior-preserving mixture fine-tuning strategy that adapts the model to new domains while retaining the learned z-axis morphological prior. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the synthesized pseudo z-stacks exhibit realistic cross-plane morphological continuity and consistently improve downstream prostate cancer classification compared with conventional 2D representations. Our results suggest that learning transferable z-axis priors from limited z-stack data provides a practical way to enrich routine pathology images with complementary morphological information. Code: this https URL.

AI.tldr: PathoS2VD generates pseudo z-stacks from single 2D histopathology images using an image-to-video latent diffusion model trained on pathology z-stack data. The synthesized stacks consistently improve downstream prostate cancer classification compared with conventional 2D representations.
AI.motivation: Thin 2D sections discard morphological cues along the z-axis, dedicated volumetric imaging is costly, and large clinical datasets lack native z-stack acquisition.
AI.method: An image-to-video latent diffusion model learns z-axis morphological priors from pathology z-stack data and synthesizes a pseudo z-stack from one 2D image. A prior-preserving mixture fine-tuning strategy adapts the model to new domains while retaining the learned z-axis prior.
AI.result: The synthesized pseudo z-stacks show realistic cross-plane morphological continuity and consistently improve downstream prostate cancer classification compared with conventional 2D representations.
AI.conclusion: Transferable z-axis priors learned from limited z-stack data offer a practical way to enrich routine pathology images with complementary morphological information.

title: FedIA: Instance-Aware Cross-Modal Representations for Federated Prompt Learning
summary: Federated Prompt Learning (FPL) enables parameter-efficient adaptation of pre-trained Vision-Language Models across decentralized clients without exchanging raw data. To cope with cross-client heterogeneity, existing FPL methods typically pair a globally shared prompt with a client-specific local prompt. However, this design personalizes only at the client level: the same local prompt is applied to all samples of a client, and the global and local prompts are combined in an input-agnostic, fixed manner. Consequently, it overlooks the substantial visual variations among samples within the same client and cannot adjust the balance between shared and personalized knowledge to each input. To address these limitations, we propose Federated Prompt Learning with Instance-Aware Cross-Modal Representations (FedIA), an FPL framework that learns instance-aware cross-modal representations. Specifically, FedIA first uses global text prompts as client-invariant semantic anchors to select image patches most relevant to each candidate class, suppressing distracting regions. The selected visual evidence then conditions the generation of instance-aware local text representations. Finally, an adaptive global-local fusion module calibrates the contributions of local and global text representations for each image-class pair. In this way, FedIA shifts personalization in FPL from the client level to the instance level while preserving the semantic knowledge shared across clients. Extensive experiments under domain shift, pathological label skew, and Dirichlet-based label skew show that FedIA outperforms FPL baselines, with maximum accuracy gains of 1.44\%-4.37\% over the latest baseline across the three settings. Ablation studies and analyses further verify the complementary contributions of instance-aware representation generation and adaptive global-local fusion.

AI.tldr: FedIA is a federated prompt learning method for vision-language models that makes personalization instance-aware rather than client-level, selecting relevant image patches per candidate class and fusing local and global text representations per input. It outperforms FPL baselines under domain shift and label skew.
AI.motivation: Existing federated prompt learning pairs a global prompt with a client-level local prompt that is applied to all samples of a client and combined in a fixed, input-agnostic way, which ignores visual variation among samples within the same client.
AI.method: Global text prompts serve as client-invariant semantic anchors that select the image patches most relevant to each candidate class, and the selected visual evidence conditions the generation of instance-aware local text representations. An adaptive global-local fusion module then calibrates the contributions of local and global text representations for each image-class pair.
AI.result: Maximum accuracy gains of 1.44% to 4.37% over the latest baseline across domain shift, pathological label skew and Dirichlet-based label skew settings, with ablations confirming the complementary contributions of the two components.
AI.conclusion: Shifting personalization from the client level to the instance level, while preserving semantic knowledge shared across clients, improves federated prompt learning.

title: MotoVerse: A Benchmark for Predictive Perception of Motorized Two-Wheelers in Dense Unstructured Traffic
summary: Motorized Two-Wheelers (MTWs) dominate personal transport across much of the Global South, yet remain largely overlooked in predictive perception research for autonomous driving and ADAS. We introduce MotoVerse, a benchmark for predictive perception from an MTW's ego-centric perspective. MotoVerse comprises 949 maneuver clips collected in dense, unstructured traffic and trajectory annotations for over 31,000 surrounding road agents, including over 16,000 MTWs, enabling two complementary tasks: Ego-Rider Maneuver Anticipation (ERMA) and Traffic Agent Trajectory Prediction (TATP). Each clip is further annotated with an MTW-specific challenge taxonomy comprising dynamic ego-motion, weak traffic structure and contextual occlusion, enabling challenge-aware evaluation. We benchmark established conventional prediction models, general-purpose Vision-Language Models (VLMs), driving-specific VLMs and vision-language-action models. Our experiments reveal three key insights: (i) video backbones reach most of their full-observation accuracy from the first fifth of a maneuver, whereas zero-shot VLMs need most of the maneuver to be observed; (ii) zero-shot VLMs, whether general-purpose or driving-specific, largely remain close to simple baselines on both tasks; a preliminary LoRA study shows that adaptation lifts anticipation sharply but leaves trajectory prediction behind conventional models; and (iii) the rider's own motion drives forecasting difficulty: for every model, including a static baseline, errors are highest during left turns and rise under dynamic ego-motion. We believe MotoVerse will serve as a challenging benchmark for safer and more robust predictive AI for intelligent two-wheelers. The dataset and evaluation code are publicly available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: MotoVerse is a benchmark for predictive perception from a motorized two-wheeler rider's viewpoint, with 949 maneuver clips and trajectory annotations for over 31,000 surrounding road agents. Zero-shot VLMs stay close to simple baselines, and the rider's own motion drives forecasting difficulty.
AI.motivation: Motorized two-wheelers dominate personal transport across much of the Global South but are largely overlooked in predictive perception research for autonomous driving and ADAS.
AI.method: The benchmark has two tasks, Ego-Rider Maneuver Anticipation and Traffic Agent Trajectory Prediction, with each clip annotated by a challenge taxonomy of dynamic ego-motion, weak traffic structure and contextual occlusion. Conventional prediction models, general-purpose and driving-specific VLMs, and vision-language-action models are benchmarked.
AI.result: Video backbones reach most of their full-observation accuracy from the first fifth of a maneuver, while zero-shot VLMs need most of the maneuver observed; zero-shot VLMs stay close to simple baselines; a preliminary LoRA study lifts anticipation sharply but leaves trajectory prediction behind conventional models; errors are highest during left turns and under dynamic ego-motion for every model, including a static baseline.
AI.conclusion: MotoVerse is presented as a challenging benchmark for safer and more robust predictive AI for intelligent two-wheelers.

title: ChanSFormer: A Channel Agnostic Vision Transformer for Multi-Channel Cell Painting Images
summary: High-content multi-channel imaging, from Cell Painting assays to remote sensing, is central to modern scientific pipelines. Because these channels are highly heterogeneous and experimental configurations frequently evolve, a practical vision backbone must be fundamentally channel-agnostic. Current channel-adaptive vision transformers rely on global self-attention with learnable channel embeddings, which can be computed only for previously known channels. Attempts to overcome this limitation of new channels either discard the embeddings, losing channel identity, or process each channel independently, thereby eliminating critical cross-channel interactions. To address this, we introduce ChanSFormer, an efficient Vision Transformer that replaces rigid embeddings with disentangled spatial-channel attention and individual channel CLS tokens. This architecture natively preserves both distinct channel identities and cross-channel information flow. Furthermore, the individual channel class token design unlocks more informative feature representations for self-supervised learning and enables representation-based channel sampling while remaining channel-agnostic. We evaluate ChanSFormer on two biology multi-channel datasets, CHAMMI, JUMP-CP and a satellite dataset, So2Sat. Experimental results show that ChanSFormer outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 3.93%-4.27% on JUMP-CP in classification accuracy. It also demonstrates exceptional cross-dataset transferability under a self-supervised setting, outperforming previous methods by up to 2.72% in accuracy in the same classification tasks. Furthermore, the disentangled attention reduces the quadratic complexity of channel-by-spatial sequence length of the global attention baseline, thus improving throughput by 55%-313%. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: ChanSFormer is a channel-agnostic Vision Transformer for multi-channel cell painting images that replaces rigid channel embeddings with disentangled spatial-channel attention and individual channel CLS tokens. It outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 3.93% to 4.27% on JUMP-CP classification and improves throughput by 55% to 313%.
AI.motivation: Channel-adaptive ViTs rely on learnable channel embeddings that exist only for previously known channels, and handling new channels either discards channel identity or processes each channel independently, losing cross-channel interactions.
AI.method: Rigid channel embeddings are replaced by disentangled spatial-channel attention and individual channel CLS tokens, which preserve channel identities and cross-channel information flow and enable representation-based channel sampling.
AI.result: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods by 3.93% to 4.27% in JUMP-CP classification accuracy, gains up to 2.72% accuracy in cross-dataset self-supervised transfer, and improves throughput by 55% to 313% over the global attention baseline. Evaluated on CHAMMI, JUMP-CP and the satellite dataset So2Sat.
AI.conclusion: Disentangled attention gives an efficient, channel-agnostic backbone for both biology and satellite multi-channel imaging.

title: METRIC-GS: Selective Metric-Scale Estimation for 3D Gaussian Splatting
summary: A 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) reconstruction inherits arbitrary units from structure-from-motion, so it cannot be measured or used to place AR content until someone supplies a scale. Both standard recipes are fragile on real captures: on five indoor scenes with tape-measured ceilings, a quantile floor-to-ceiling heuristic errs by 27% and metric-depth alignment by 35-71% across three networks. We present METRIC-GS, a selective scale estimator for real indoor photographs: it reads the scale off the reconstruction's own semantic content and, just as importantly, refuses when the evidence is thin. A frozen 2D teacher labels Gaussians by visibility-aware voting; instance-level size priors for architectural and furniture classes (doors, tables, the floor-to-ceiling gap) are fused by a robust maximum-likelihood step; and an inlier-mass test turns thin evidence into an explicit abstention that doubles as a router to a heavyweight metric model. On 47 ScanNet++ scenes with laser ground truth, with a configuration frozen before public evaluation, the estimator alone cuts the heuristic's mean error from 21.1% to 16.6% (9.3% on the 28 scenes it acts on) at ~11 s per scene. MASt3R remains the more accurate standalone estimator (9.9%), but routing only our refusals to it matches running it everywhere with 60% fewer invocations; this selective hybrid is the configuration we advocate. Visibility-aware voting raises the scenes the estimator can act on from 16 to 28 at unchanged deployed accuracy. Applied unchanged to 13 phone and drone captures of our own, on which MASt3R fails its own registration gate 12 times, the system improves all five captures it acts on and degrades none. We also report that a current feed-forward metric model scores 2.3% on a benchmark inside its training mixture and 28-35% on captures it has never seen: a published metric-scale number is a best case, not a deployment estimate.

AI.tldr: METRIC-GS is a selective metric-scale estimator for 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions of indoor scenes that reads scale from semantic content and abstains when the evidence is thin, routing those cases to a heavier metric model. On 47 ScanNet++ scenes it reduces the heuristic's mean error from 21.1% to 16.6%.
AI.motivation: Structure-from-motion reconstructions carry arbitrary units, and standard scale recipes are fragile: a floor-to-ceiling quantile heuristic errs by 27% and metric-depth alignment by 35% to 71% across three networks on five indoor scenes.
AI.method: A frozen 2D teacher labels Gaussians by visibility-aware voting, instance-level size priors for architectural and furniture classes are fused by a robust maximum-likelihood step, and an inlier-mass test turns thin evidence into explicit abstention that also routes to a heavyweight metric model.
AI.result: On 47 ScanNet++ scenes with laser ground truth, the estimator alone cuts the heuristic's mean error from 21.1% to 16.6% (9.3% on the 28 scenes it acts on) at about 11 s per scene. MASt3R is more accurate standalone (9.9%), but routing only the refusals to it matches running it everywhere with 60% fewer invocations. Visibility-aware voting raises actionable scenes from 16 to 28, and the system improves all five of its 13 phone and drone captures that it acts on. A feed-forward metric model scores 2.3% on a benchmark inside its training mixture and 28% to 35% on unseen captures.
AI.conclusion: A published metric-scale number is a best case rather than a deployment estimate, and selective abstention with routing gives a deployable hybrid.

title: USI-Brain: Enhancing Underwater Spatial Intelligence via Spatial Data-Driven Vision-Language Modeling
summary: Underwater spatial reasoning depends on object boundaries and geometric cues that are obscured by scattering, color distortion, and low visibility. Existing underwater resources capture these cues through images, annotations, and depth maps, but provide fragmented supervision for vision-language models. We present a spatial data engine that connects visual appearance with object-level geometry through enhancement, 2D and geometry-assisted question generation, and expert filtering. It produces 4.27M QA pairs across five capability groups. We use this corpus to train USI-Brain and introduce an Underwater Prior-guided Rectifier (UPR) that applies gated corrections to visual features. USI-Bench evaluates the resulting capabilities with 6,525 held-out QA pairs. On its 15 task metrics, USI-Brain and USI-Brain + UPR improve over Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct by 5.76 and 7.63 points on average, respectively, using signed differences on 100-point scales. Ablations show that geometry-assisted supervision improves depth and ordering by 4.8 and 6.1 points with UPR disabled, while UPR adds 18.0 points in scene description under matched training data. Both variants use raw images at evaluation. Across NautData, UWBench, and MarineEval, USI-Brain achieves the best or joint-best score on 28 of 32 metrics. Model weights and USI-Bench will be released at this https URL.

AI.tldr: USI-Brain is a vision-language model for underwater spatial reasoning, trained on a 4.27M-pair QA corpus from a spatial data engine that links visual appearance with object-level geometry. It improves over Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct on the 15 task metrics of USI-Bench.
AI.motivation: Underwater spatial reasoning depends on object boundaries and geometric cues obscured by scattering, color distortion and low visibility, and existing underwater resources give fragmented supervision for vision-language models.
AI.method: A spatial data engine combines enhancement, 2D and geometry-assisted question generation and expert filtering to produce 4.27M QA pairs across five capability groups. USI-Brain is trained on this corpus and adds an Underwater Prior-guided Rectifier (UPR) that applies gated corrections to visual features.
AI.result: On the 15 USI-Bench task metrics, USI-Brain and USI-Brain + UPR improve over Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct by 5.76 and 7.63 points on average. Geometry-assisted supervision improves depth and ordering by 4.8 and 6.1 points with UPR disabled, UPR adds 18.0 points in scene description, and across NautData, UWBench and MarineEval the model is best or joint-best on 28 of 32 metrics. Both variants use raw images at evaluation.
AI.conclusion: Geometry-aware supervision and prior-guided rectification of visual features together yield a stronger underwater spatial reasoning model.

title: UniRestorer++: Scalable Universal Image Restoration with Multi-Granularity Degradation Modeling
summary: Universal image restoration aims to handle diverse degradations within a single model, but a reliable scaling strategy remains underexplored. Increasing backbone depth and width can lead to performance saturation, while degradation-aware specialization depends on accurate degradation estimation and is vulnerable to errors on out-of-distribution and real-world inputs. We propose UniRestorer++, a scalable framework based on multi-granularity degradation modeling. It progressively refines degradation groups and introduces group-specific experts, coupling capacity growth with specialization. Degradation-estimation-based routing selects a root-to-leaf path, while granularity-estimation-based routing chooses a level along that path to balance specialization and robustness. Spatially dense degradation representation maps further enable region-aware routing for spatially non-uniform corruptions. We develop CDD-50, a benchmark covering 50 degradation categories from single to penta-degradation. Experiments show approximately log-linear PSNR trends over the evaluated model-size range and stronger scaling gains on out-of-distribution and real-world data than vanilla MoE scaling. UniRestorer++ achieves state-of-the-art performance across benchmarks and demonstrates zero-shot generalization and few-shot transfer on real-world images. Code: this https URL

AI.tldr: UniRestorer++ is a scalable universal image restoration framework that uses multi-granularity degradation modeling with group-specific experts, and it reports approximately log-linear PSNR gains over the evaluated model-size range.
AI.motivation: Universal restoration models saturate when backbone depth and width grow, and degradation-aware specialization is fragile because degradation estimation is unreliable on out-of-distribution and real-world inputs.
AI.method: Degradation groups are progressively refined into a hierarchy with a group-specific expert for each node; degradation-estimation routing selects a root-to-leaf path, granularity-estimation routing chooses a level along that path, and spatially dense degradation maps enable region-aware routing for non-uniform corruptions; the authors also build the CDD-50 benchmark with 50 degradation categories from single to penta-degradation.
AI.result: PSNR follows approximately log-linear trends over the evaluated model-size range, with stronger scaling gains on out-of-distribution and real-world data than vanilla MoE scaling; the model achieves state-of-the-art performance across benchmarks and shows zero-shot generalization and few-shot transfer on real-world images.
AI.conclusion: Coupling capacity growth with degradation-aware specialization offers a more reliable scaling strategy for universal image restoration than enlarging a single model or using a vanilla mixture of experts.

title: DeepfakeGenome: Toward Next-Generation Deepfake Attribution
summary: In recent years, AIGC technologies are capable of generating hyper-realistic forged facial images, posing severe threats to facial security safety. To tackle these challenges, early Deepfake research primarily centered on real-fake classification. Recently, growing efforts have been devoted to the Deepfake Attribution (DFA) of generated content. Nevertheless, existing research on Deepfake detection and attribution faces saturated performance in binary classification, limited diversity in datasets and algorithms, and imperfect evaluation protocols, which severely impede practical application. To address these limitations, we propose a comprehensive deepfake detection and attribution benchmark named DeepfakeGenome (DFG). It contains 100 facial forgery algorithms and 2M images in total, achieving 4x to 100x larger than prior DFA benchmarks. We further design 4 protocols for practical evaluation, including a novel retrieval-based attribution paradigm. Unlike previous open-set evaluation metrics, the proposed retrieval metrics are more aligned with the real-world active defense situation of blacklist registration mechanisms. Based on these elaborate designs, we investigate the performance ceiling of deepfake attribution task. Over 2k experimental evaluations are conducted, and 10 insightful findings are derived. We believe this work can provide new insights into the DFA research field. The Code and Benchmark of DFG are avaliable on this https URL.

AI.tldr: DeepfakeGenome is a deepfake detection and attribution benchmark with 100 facial forgery algorithms and 2M images, evaluated under four protocols including a retrieval-based attribution paradigm, and more than 2k experiments yield 10 findings.
AI.motivation: Deepfake detection and attribution research is saturated in binary classification, has limited dataset and algorithm diversity, and relies on imperfect evaluation protocols that do not reflect practical use.
AI.method: The benchmark contains 100 facial forgery algorithms and 2M images, 4x to 100x larger than prior attribution benchmarks; four evaluation protocols are designed, including a retrieval-based attribution paradigm whose retrieval metrics align with blacklist registration in active defense, unlike previous open-set metrics.
AI.result: Over 2k experimental evaluations probe the performance ceiling of deepfake attribution and yield 10 insightful findings.
AI.conclusion: The benchmark and its protocols are offered as a basis for new insights into the deepfake attribution field.

title: RI-Prune: Relation and Information Aware Visual Token Pruning for Multi-Image Vision-Language Models
summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have recently been extended to handle multiple input images, but this extension dramatically increases the visual token budget, making visual-token pruning not merely an efficiency option but a practical necessity. Existing visual-token pruning methods, primarily designed for the single-image setting, rely on attention-derived saliency signals to estimate per-token importance. However, this attention-centric design transfers poorly to the multi-image regime: it causes substantial performance degradation on multi-image benchmarks, suffers from strong positional bias, and loses discriminative attention signals as the number of input images increases. To test whether attention-selected tokens are truly important for multi-image reasoning, we conduct two complementary causal probes Leave-One-In and Leave-One-Deletion, which measure token importance by restoring individual tokens to a zeroed visual sequence or removing them from the full sequence. Attention-based pruners provide only marginal gains over random selection, showing that attention is a weak proxy for visual-token importance in multi-image reasoning. Motivated by this gap, we propose Relation and Information Aware Pruning (RI-Prune), a training-free, attention-free pre-decoder selector for multi-image visual token pruning. RI-Prune scores each visual token using a z-normalized combination of three signals computed from projector outputs: query relevance, cross-image correspondence with compact per-image prototypes, and intra image representativeness. By integrating these signals, RI-Prune performs balanced per-image Top-K selection to preserve information across input images. Across multiple multi-image benchmarks and three LVLM backbones, RI-Prune achieves a stronger trade-off between token reduction and task performance than prior pruning methods, particularly under aggressive token budgets.

AI.tldr: RI-Prune is a training-free, attention-free visual token pruning method for multi-image vision-language models that scores tokens by query relevance, cross-image correspondence and intra-image representativeness.
AI.motivation: Attention-based visual token pruners designed for single images transfer poorly to multi-image inputs, degrading performance, showing positional bias, and giving only marginal gains over random selection in causal probes.
AI.method: Two causal probes, Leave-One-In and Leave-One-Deletion, measure token importance; RI-Prune computes three signals from projector outputs (query relevance, cross-image correspondence with compact per-image prototypes, and intra-image representativeness), combines them as a z-normalized score, and performs balanced per-image Top-K selection before the decoder.
AI.result: Across multiple multi-image benchmarks and three LVLM backbones, RI-Prune achieves a stronger trade-off between token reduction and task performance than prior pruning methods, particularly under aggressive token budgets.
AI.conclusion: Attention is a weak proxy for visual token importance in multi-image reasoning, and a pre-decoder, attention-free selector preserves information across images more effectively.

title: RouTex: Multi-reference 3D Texture Generation by Reprogramming Rotary Position Encoding
summary: While single-image 3D texture generation has advanced significantly, conditioning texture synthesis on multi-view reference images remains largely under-explored, despite its necessity for resolving surface ambiguity in unobserved regions. In this paper, we propose RouTex, a novel multi-reference 3D texture generation framework based on in-context Diffusion Transformers (DiT). Our key insight is that native 3D Rotary Position Encoding (RoPE) inherently possesses spatial addressing capabilities. We introduce Positional Routing (PR) to reprogram 3D RoPE along spatial and semantic dimensions, establishing explicit reference-to-view correspondence without introducing additional parameters. To execute this routing efficiently, Dual-Granularity Attention (DGA) combines per-view local attention for fine texture fidelity with global joint attention over deduplicated references for cross-view consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RouTex achieves new state-of-the-art performance in multi-reference 3D texture generation.

AI.tldr: RouTex is a multi-reference 3D texture generation framework that reprograms 3D rotary position encoding in an in-context diffusion transformer to establish reference-to-view correspondence without extra parameters.
AI.motivation: Single-image 3D texture generation is well studied, but conditioning on multi-view reference images is under-explored, although it is needed to resolve surface ambiguity in unobserved regions.
AI.method: Positional Routing reprograms 3D RoPE along spatial and semantic dimensions to create explicit reference-to-view correspondence with no additional parameters; Dual-Granularity Attention combines per-view local attention for texture fidelity with global joint attention over deduplicated references for cross-view consistency.
AI.result: The abstract reports that RouTex achieves new state-of-the-art performance in multi-reference 3D texture generation, without giving specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Native 3D RoPE has spatial addressing capacity that can be repurposed for multi-reference conditioning, giving an efficient route to consistent texture synthesis.

title: SleuthVLM: Do We Really Need Audio-in-Video for Omni Video Understanding?
summary: Omni models answer questions about videos by jointly processing sampled frames and audio in one turn, with progress driven largely by scaling model size and omni training data. We ask whether a model needs to hear the audio directly at all, and present SleuthVLM, an agent harness built on a VLM that never hears the audio directly: speech will be transcribed into text, and the VLM will sleuth the video on its own without any predefined workflow. On four omni benchmarks with videos up to 90 minutes, SleuthVLM achieves the best average accuracy: \textbf{75.0%}, 2.6 points above Gemini 3.8 Flash, and it also tops the Video-MME-v2 leaderboard with \textbf{77.8%}; with an open-source 27B VLM, it beats all open-source omni models. We draw three findings: SleuthVLM beats a model that glances; hearing is not the bottleneck, agentic ability is; omni understanding needs better agentic ability, not just more omni data for modality alignment. So we provide a simple but effective starting point for doing omni video understanding. Omni understanding needs better agents, not just bigger models that hear.

AI.tldr: SleuthVLM is an agent harness on a VLM that never hears the audio: speech is transcribed to text and the model investigates the video agentically, reaching 75.0% average accuracy on four omni benchmarks and 77.8% on Video-MME-v2.
AI.motivation: Omni models jointly process sampled frames and audio, with progress driven mainly by model scale and omni training data, and the authors ask whether a model needs to hear the audio directly at all.
AI.method: SleuthVLM is an agent harness built on a VLM that receives transcribed speech as text and explores the video on its own without any predefined workflow.
AI.result: On four omni benchmarks with videos up to 90 minutes, SleuthVLM achieves the best average accuracy of 75.0%, 2.6 points above Gemini 3.8 Flash, and tops the Video-MME-v2 leaderboard with 77.8%; with an open-source 27B VLM it beats all open-source omni models.
AI.conclusion: Hearing is not the bottleneck and agentic ability is, so omni video understanding needs better agents rather than more omni data for modality alignment.

title: GeoBiaset: A Counterfactual Benchmark for Demographic Bias in World-Level Geolocalization
comment: Accepted at Neurips 2026, E&D track. Project page: this https URL
summary: World-level image geolocalization is an increasingly important task, yet the biases of current models remain poorly understood. Prior work has identified coarse dataset imbalances noting, for instance, that some cities are absent from training sets and that models tend to perform better in wealthier regions. However, no one has yet examined which visual cues drive these disparities. To do so, we introduce GeoBiaset, the first benchmark designed to measure how geolocalization models are influenced by the apparent race of a person inserted into the image foreground. The dataset consists of 9,541 images, pairing existing geotagged background images with counterfactual edits spanning seven races, holding the ground-truth coordinates fixed. Controlled masking experiments show that occlusion and background drift do not fully explain geolocalization degradation. Alongside the benchmark, we introduce the Person-Origin Perturbation Indicators (POPI), novel metrics that quantify model resilience to these demographic perturbations by measuring whether predictions are pulled toward the region associated with the inserted group. Our evaluation of state-of-the-art geolocalization and multimodal large language models reveals a 16-47% drop in continent-level performance when a subject from a demographically mismatched group is inserted. A landmark versus no-landmark analysis and gradient-weighted heatmaps show that models preferentially attend to geographic landmarks when present, but shift attention to facial features in their absence.

AI.tldr: GeoBiaset is a counterfactual benchmark of 9,541 images that inserts people of seven races into geotagged backgrounds to measure demographic bias in world-level geolocalization, and it introduces the POPI metrics.
AI.motivation: Prior work has documented coarse dataset imbalances in geolocalization, but no study had examined which visual cues drive the disparities, in particular how the apparent race of a foreground person affects predictions.
AI.method: Existing geotagged backgrounds are paired with counterfactual edits that insert a person of one of seven races while holding the ground-truth coordinates fixed; controlled masking experiments test occlusion and background drift; the Person-Origin Perturbation Indicators (POPI) measure whether predictions are pulled toward the region associated with the inserted group; landmark versus no-landmark analysis and gradient-weighted heatmaps probe attention.
AI.result: State-of-the-art geolocalization and multimodal LLMs show a 16-47% drop in continent-level performance when a subject from a demographically mismatched group is inserted; occlusion and background drift do not fully explain the degradation; models attend to geographic landmarks when present and shift to facial features when absent.
AI.conclusion: Geolocalization models are influenced by the apparent race of an inserted person, an effect that occlusion and background change alone do not explain, so this resilience must be measured directly.

title: STARE: Scene Text-Aware multimodal Retrieval for Everyday objects
summary: In this study, we focus on service robots that retrieve and transport everyday objects based on free-form instructions that may refer to visual features and scene text. This is challenging because it requires a multimodal understanding of the visual features and spatial relationships of objects, as well as scene text embedded in the environment. To address this, we propose Scene Text-Aware multimodal Retrieval for Everyday objects (STARE), which leverages visual and textual cues in response to free-form instructions. STARE introduces Crosslingual Visual Prompt to enhance scene text interpretation, and models the complex relationships between named entities in the instructions and their corresponding objects. We evaluate STARE using two novel benchmarks, GoGetIt and TextCaps-test, both of which consist of real-world indoor/outdoor images and instructions involving object manipulation and navigation. The results show that STARE outperforms all baseline methods on standard multimodal retrieval metrics. Furthermore, in physical experiments conducted under a zero-shot transfer setting, STARE achieves an overall success rate of 80%. Our project page and code are provided in the Supplementary Materials.

AI.tldr: STARE is a scene text-aware multimodal retrieval model for service robots that retrieves everyday objects from free-form instructions and achieves an 80% success rate in zero-shot physical experiments.
AI.motivation: Service robots must interpret free-form instructions that refer to visual features and scene text, which requires joint understanding of object appearance, spatial relations and text embedded in the environment.
AI.method: STARE combines visual and textual cues from the instruction, introduces a Crosslingual Visual Prompt to improve scene text interpretation, and models relations between named entities in the instruction and their corresponding objects; it is evaluated on two new benchmarks, GoGetIt and TextCaps-test.
AI.result: STARE outperforms all baseline methods on standard multimodal retrieval metrics, and in physical experiments under a zero-shot transfer setting it achieves an overall success rate of 80%.
AI.conclusion: Combining visual and scene-text cues with entity-level relations lets robots retrieve objects from instructions that refer to text in the scene.

title: Many Pixels, One Composition: Self-Supervised Spectra for Specimen-Level Prediction
summary: Can hyperspectral (HS) imaging be used to predict the elemental composition of physical specimens found on the Earth's surface? We approach this problem as a supervised regression task, using an open dataset of specimens, each comprising a HS cube and elemental characterization. In particular, we train an encoder in a self-supervised fashion that operates on pixel-level; then freeze the encoder and train a lightweight attention-based regression head in a supervised manner, by pairing many representations of a given specimen with its corresponding elemental label. In test specimens, our approach significantly outperforms traditional spectral matching and unmixing baselines. It also outperforms supervised learning models based on the mean spectrum (of similar model capacity), while full model fine-tuning achieves the strongest performance, at substantially higher model capacity.

AI.tldr: The paper predicts the elemental composition of specimens from hyperspectral cubes by training a self-supervised pixel-level encoder and then a lightweight attention regression head on many pixel representations per specimen.
AI.motivation: Predicting elemental composition from hyperspectral imagery of surface specimens is a supervised regression problem, and the abstract positions spectral matching, unmixing and mean-spectrum models as baselines that this approach must beat.
AI.method: A pixel-level encoder is trained in a self-supervised fashion; the encoder is then frozen and a lightweight attention-based regression head is trained by pairing many pixel representations of a specimen with its elemental label.
AI.result: On test specimens the approach significantly outperforms traditional spectral matching and unmixing baselines and supervised models based on the mean spectrum of similar capacity; full model fine-tuning achieves the strongest performance at substantially higher capacity.
AI.conclusion: Aggregating many self-supervised pixel representations per specimen is an effective route to specimen-level composition prediction, with full fine-tuning giving the best accuracy at a higher capacity cost.

title: XuanJian-DINOSAR: A SAR Foundation Model Based on Global and Local Semantic Consistency
summary: Self-supervised pre-training on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery enables transferable representations, but the optical-SAR domain gap and speckle perturbations limit representation stability. Most SAR foundation models use masked image modeling (MIM) through pixel reconstruction or structural feature prediction, which is sensitive to speckle or relies on predefined operators. Joint modeling of cross-view semantics and perturbation stability at corresponding spatial locations remains underexplored. We propose XuanJian-DINOSAR, a SAR foundation model based on global and local semantic consistency. We curate over 360K publicly available SAR target chips, detection images, and scene images spanning diverse targets, scenes, and sensors, and adapt an optically pre-trained DINOv2 model to SAR through self-supervised learning. The framework combines DINO global semantic self-distillation, iBOT local masked modeling, and KoLeo feature-distribution regularization to learn globally discriminative and locally structure-aware representations. We introduce a local semantic consistency branch tailored to SAR intensity statistics and coherent imaging characteristics. Shared geometric transformations produce spatially aligned teacher weak views and student strong views. Intensity transformations and Gamma multiplicative speckle perturbations are applied to student views, while a cosine consistency loss aligns patch tokens at corresponding locations, promoting stability under radiometric perturbations. This objective complements the cross-region and cross-scale semantic consistency of DINOv2 multi-crop training, jointly enforcing global and local semantic consistency. Experiments on multiple downstream classification and detection datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on most evaluation metrics, validating the generality and transferability of the learned representations.

AI.tldr: XuanJian-DINOSAR is a SAR foundation model built by adapting an optically pre-trained DINOv2 with self-supervised learning on over 360K SAR chips and images, with a local semantic consistency branch for speckle stability.
AI.motivation: Masked image modeling for SAR relies on pixel reconstruction or predefined structural operators that are sensitive to speckle, and joint modeling of cross-view semantics and perturbation stability at corresponding locations remains underexplored given the optical-SAR domain gap.
AI.method: The model combines DINO global self-distillation, iBOT local masked modeling and KoLeo feature-distribution regularization, plus a local semantic consistency branch in which spatially aligned teacher weak views and student strong views receive Gamma multiplicative speckle and intensity perturbations, and a cosine loss aligns patch tokens at corresponding locations.
AI.result: Experiments on multiple downstream classification and detection datasets show state-of-the-art performance on most evaluation metrics.
AI.conclusion: Jointly enforcing global and local semantic consistency yields representations that are general, transferable and stable under radiometric perturbations in SAR imagery.

title: Semantic Prior-Guided Incomplete Cross-Modal Retrieval with Noisy Labels
summary: Cross-modal retrieval (CMR) aims to bridge the semantic gaps between modalities by learning shared representations. Unfortunately, due to the dynamism and inconsistencies in real-world data acquisition, multimodal datasets frequently encounter severe modality incompleteness. Existing incomplete CMR methods adhere to a label-driven paradigm, relying heavily on categorical annotations as the semantic benchmark. However, label noise is difficult to avoid and often coexists with modality incompleteness. To address this challenge, we propose a novel semantic prior-guided framework for incomplete cross-modal retrieval with noisy labels, termed SPIRN. Specifically, SPIRN uses fixed semantic priors as a consistent reference for robust representation learning, noisy-label handling, and missing-modality completion. Based on this reference, Semantic Priors Guidance (SPG) establishes a stable category-level semantic space, Quality-aware Robust Learning (QRL) dynamically evaluates sample quality to distinguish clean samples from noisy ones and handles noise via reverse learning, Prior-guided Global Label Calibration (PGLC) rectifies corrupted annotations for refined supervision, and Confidence-driven Selective Imputation (CSI) recovers missing modalities from a cross-modal memory bank while filtering unreliable imputations with an increasing threshold. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first framework to jointly tackle the dual challenges of modality incompleteness and label noise in the CMR community. Extensive experiments on four widely used benchmark datasets demonstrate that SPIRN outperforms 11 state-of-the-art methods in various scenarios involving both missing modalities and noisy labels.

AI.tldr: SPIRN is a semantic prior-guided framework for incomplete cross-modal retrieval with noisy labels, using fixed semantic priors as a consistent reference to handle missing modalities and label noise jointly.
AI.motivation: Existing incomplete cross-modal retrieval methods rely heavily on categorical labels as the semantic benchmark, but label noise is hard to avoid and often coexists with modality incompleteness.
AI.method: Fixed semantic priors serve as a reference for four components: Semantic Priors Guidance builds a stable category-level semantic space, Quality-aware Robust Learning scores sample quality to separate clean from noisy samples and handles noise via reverse learning, Prior-guided Global Label Calibration corrects corrupted annotations, and Confidence-driven Selective Imputation recovers missing modalities from a cross-modal memory bank with an increasing filtering threshold.
AI.result: On four widely used benchmark datasets, SPIRN outperforms 11 state-of-the-art methods in scenarios involving both missing modalities and noisy labels.
AI.conclusion: It is presented as the first framework to tackle modality incompleteness and label noise jointly in cross-modal retrieval, with the priors serving as a consistent reference throughout.

title: ReactWorld: Structuring Interaction Responses for Embodied Video Generation
comment: 10 pages, 7 figures. Project page: this https URL
summary: Embodied video world models predict scene changes caused by robot actions, yet generated object responses may remain inconsistent with task intent and contact dynamics. Critical responses in embodied scenes often concentrate in local regions and specific time intervals. Inspired by chain-of-thought reasoning, we introduce ReactWorld, an embodied video generation model guided by structured interaction anticipation. In the generation backbone's feature space, an interaction response field predictor anticipates how the interaction will unfold, explicitly describing participant roles, future motion response intensity, and local motion changes. A response feedback adapter forms increments to object features from the difference between the object branch's outputs with predicted and zeroed local dynamics inputs. It also converts predicted displacements into positional biases for temporal attention. These two mechanisms guide object feature updates and information retrieval across frames, respectively. Through interaction anticipation and generative feedback, ReactWorld achieves an average score of 77.51 on RBench, outperforming PhysisForcing by 3.29 points with improvements in all nine categories. On EZS-Bench, it achieves a Domain score of 86.98 and an average score of 81.87.

AI.tldr: ReactWorld is an embodied video generation model that anticipates structured interaction responses through an interaction response field predictor and a response feedback adapter, reaching an average RBench score of 77.51.
AI.motivation: Embodied video world models predict scene changes caused by robot actions, but generated object responses can be inconsistent with task intent and contact dynamics, even though critical responses concentrate in local regions and time intervals.
AI.method: In the backbone's feature space, an interaction response field predictor anticipates participant roles, future motion response intensity and local motion changes; a response feedback adapter forms increments to object features from the difference between outputs with predicted and zeroed local dynamics inputs, and converts predicted displacements into positional biases for temporal attention.
AI.result: ReactWorld achieves an average score of 77.51 on RBench, outperforming PhysisForcing by 3.29 points with improvements in all nine categories; on EZS-Bench it achieves a Domain score of 86.98 and an average score of 81.87.
AI.conclusion: Structured interaction anticipation combined with generative feedback improves how object responses follow task intent and contact dynamics in embodied video generation.

title: RDT-3D: Resolution-Decoupled Training for High-Fidelity 3D Geometry Generation
summary: High-fidelity 3D geometry generation requires maintaining global structural coherence alongside fine-grained surface details. While recent coarse-to-fine frameworks leverage Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) to condition local queries, we reveal a critical training-inference resolution discrepancy: coordinate guidance and geometric supervision are aligned during training, whereas inference decodes high-resolution geometry from coarse spatial coordinates. This mismatch introduces a severe distribution shift that degrades fine details. To overcome this, we propose Resolution-Decoupled Training (RDT), which anchors RoPE guidance at 512 resolution while supervising geometry at 1536, enabling robust detail extrapolation. Additionally, to eliminate high-resolution data bottlenecks, we present Dual3D-300K, a large-scale paired dataset comprising 300K watertight 3D point clouds explicitly aligned across 512 and 1536 resolutions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RDT substantially improves sharp geometric regions, while Dual3D-300K offers a scalable benchmark for high-resolution 3D generation.

AI.tldr: RDT-3D proposes Resolution-Decoupled Training, which anchors RoPE guidance at 512 resolution while supervising geometry at 1536, and releases Dual3D-300K, a paired dataset of 300K watertight point clouds at both resolutions.
AI.motivation: Coarse-to-fine 3D generation uses RoPE to condition local queries, but training aligns coordinate guidance with supervision while inference decodes high-resolution geometry from coarse coordinates, a mismatch that causes distribution shift and degrades fine details; high-resolution data is also a bottleneck.
AI.method: Resolution-Decoupled Training anchors RoPE guidance at 512 while supervising geometry at 1536; Dual3D-300K provides 300K watertight 3D point clouds explicitly aligned across the 512 and 1536 resolutions.
AI.result: Experiments show that RDT substantially improves sharp geometric regions; the abstract gives no numeric scores.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling the guidance and supervision resolutions enables robust detail extrapolation, and Dual3D-300K offers a scalable benchmark for high-resolution 3D generation.

title: PTQ4SAM3: Semantics-Preserving Post-Training Quantization for Segment Anything Model 3
comment: 15 pages, 4 figures. Accepted to WACV 2027. Includes supplementary material
summary: Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM 3) can segment objects from text prompts and track them across video, but its memory and computation costs make deployment difficult. Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces these costs by using fewer bits. However, a quantized model can select the wrong object or lose track of its target across frames. We call this prompt-alignment drift. Controlled tests show that perturbing low-variance feature directions strongly affects target selection. We propose Semantics-Preserving Quantization (SPQ), which gives more calibration weight to concept-sensitive parameters, preserves residual features, and corrects the mean error in video memory. Fixed text concepts guide calibration without task annotations. All three components operate offline and add no inference operators. With a W4A8 image encoder, SPQ improves RefCOCO Pr@0.5 from 42.1 to 72.5 over PTQ4SAM while retaining 54.8 COCO mask AP. Experiments on LVIS, RefCOCO variants, and SA-V show consistent gains. A CLIP study also shows improved image-text retrieval.

AI.tldr: SPQ is a semantics-preserving post-training quantization method for SAM 3 that keeps text-prompted object selection and video tracking aligned under quantization, improving RefCOCO Pr@0.5 from 42.1 to 72.5 with a W4A8 image encoder.
AI.motivation: SAM 3 is costly to deploy, and quantized models can select the wrong object or lose track of it across frames, a failure the authors call prompt-alignment drift.
AI.method: Controlled tests show that perturbing low-variance feature directions strongly affects target selection; SPQ gives more calibration weight to concept-sensitive parameters, preserves residual features and corrects the mean error in video memory, using fixed text concepts to guide calibration without task annotations, and all components run offline and add no inference operators.
AI.result: With a W4A8 image encoder, SPQ improves RefCOCO Pr@0.5 from 42.1 to 72.5 over PTQ4SAM while retaining 54.8 COCO mask AP; experiments on LVIS, RefCOCO variants and SA-V show consistent gains, and a CLIP study shows improved image-text retrieval.
AI.conclusion: Preserving prompt alignment during quantization avoids wrong-object selection and tracking loss without adding inference cost.

title: DSRS: Teaching MLLMs to Perceive, Reason, and Segment in Complex Driving Scenes
summary: Existing reasoning segmentation frameworks typically employ multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with broad world knowledge to extract semantics in a human-like manner and generate corresponding segmentation masks. Nevertheless, these frameworks lack the necessary scene-specific awareness. This paper introduces driving scene reasoning segmentation (DSRS), a scene-specific task that requires models to interpret implicit instructions, infer spatial relations, detect potential risks, handle challenging conditions, and comprehend underlying traffic rules, ultimately generating accurate segmentation masks. Meanwhile, we establish a benchmark dataset to facilitate future research on the DSRS task. To pioneer this task, we propose DSRS-Net, a novel architecture with advanced reasoning segmentation capability for automated driving. Specifically, DSRS-Net seamlessly infuses geometric features for deeper reasoning segmentation, without compromising the original multimodal fusion mechanism. This strategy effectively mitigates the modality representation mismatch in MLLMs caused by RGB-only pretraining, while enhancing the integration of geometric, contextual, and linguistic features. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of DSRS-Net in both driving scene reasoning segmentation and other language-driven segmentation tasks across various public datasets. The source code and dataset will be released upon publication.

AI.tldr: DSRS introduces driving scene reasoning segmentation, a task and benchmark for generating masks from implicit instructions in complex driving scenes, together with DSRS-Net, which infuses geometric features into an MLLM.
AI.motivation: Reasoning segmentation frameworks built on MLLMs lack the scene-specific awareness needed for driving, such as inferring spatial relations, risks, challenging conditions and traffic rules, and RGB-only pretraining causes a modality representation mismatch.
AI.method: DSRS-Net infuses geometric features for deeper reasoning segmentation without compromising the original multimodal fusion mechanism, integrating geometric, contextual and linguistic features, and a benchmark dataset is established for the DSRS task.
AI.result: The authors report superior performance of DSRS-Net on driving scene reasoning segmentation and on other language-driven segmentation tasks across various public datasets; the abstract gives no numbers.
AI.conclusion: Geometric infusion mitigates the RGB-pretraining mismatch for scene-specific driving reasoning, and the source code and dataset will be released upon publication.

title: Rohbau3D-Semantics: Dense Semantic and Instance Labels for Point Clouds of Indoor Shell Construction Scenes
comment: Accepted at the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027)
summary: We present the Rohbau3D-Semantics dataset, which adds dense semantic and instance-level labels to laser scans of the previously released Rohbau3D domain data from shell construction sites. The dataset comprises 504 point cloud scenes from 14 survey sites, each captured with a terrestrial laser scanner and stored in a scanner-centered local coordinate system. Unlike point clouds sampled from reconstructed meshes or synthetic building models, the data preserve the characteristic properties of real laser scanning, including non-uniform sampling, measurement artifacts, reflections, and fine geometric detail. Combined with manual labels, expert oversight during pointwise annotation, and full-scene review, this yields a high-quality benchmark for semantic scene understanding in complex built environments. The dataset includes 17 class labels of building components and one background class, along with instance annotations for object-level analysis. In addition to the 3D point clouds, the release also provides scripts for deriving geometrically aligned panoramic and cube-map representations of color, LiDAR reflection intensity, depth, surface normals, semantic labels, and instance labels from the 3D arrays. We describe the acquisition pipeline, annotation protocol, quality-control process, and panorama-generation procedure, and provide benchmark splits and baseline experiments for semantic segmentation. By combining precise terrestrial laser scans, dense annotations, and a wide variety of shell-construction scenes, Rohbau3D-Semantics bridges the gap among synthetic indoor datasets, mesh-derived benchmarks, and smaller construction-specific resources. The dataset is intended to support research on 3D scene understanding, construction-site analytics, and multimodal scene analysis in the built environment. Access and download the full dataset via this https URL

AI.tldr: Rohbau3D-Semantics adds dense semantic and instance labels to 504 terrestrial laser scans of indoor shell construction sites, with 17 building component classes plus background, and provides panorama and cube-map derivation scripts with baseline segmentation experiments.
